body.claim: Derives an authorized_action from a signed tool classification fact, so a semantic identity minted from a classified tool call is re-derivable offline from signed facts plus this versioned rule alone.
verifier_obligations: The (connector_identity, canonical_tool_name) in the classification fact MUST appear in keel.permit.value_movement_classification at the referenced classification_artifact_version, and that artifact's digest MUST equal classification_artifact_digest. Re-derivation is thus fully offline and does not trust the issuer's classification result.
control.mode MUST be enforced_in_path. An observed (not in-path) call never derives a payment authorized_action; enforcement qualifies issuance, it does not define the action.

The derived authorized_action feeds the existing semantic selector as action_name/operation = payment.execute. The permit's own invocation.operation stays call.tools; the two are distinct signed facts, not competing descriptions of one field.

transport_surface and target_surface are recorded separately. target_surface = payment_rail describes the action's resource class; it is NOT a claim that the wire was a native payment-rail integration.
No provider outcome, settlement, or completion is implied. payment.execute is authority to attempt; observed_evidence carries what actually happened.
body.non_authorizing: This rule governs presentation identity only. It never affects policy evaluation, dispatch, executable authority, or verdicts. A wrong derivation degrades a title; it cannot escalate authorization.
